17. Mr. Siddique has further pointed out that sections 32 to 46 in Chapter-V of the Act, 1950 have provided for preparation of compensation assessment roll and acquisition of rent receiving interests. Section 46 has provided for modification of the record-of-rights prepared under Chapter-IV by eliminating the entire chain of interest or rent receivers and then for reprint and distribution of the record-of-rights. Section 144 and subsequently added section 144A (inserted by amendment, 1967) of the Act in Part-V, Chapter XVII has provided for revision of the record-of-rights and a presumption of correctness has been attached to the revised record-of-rights. Section 152 has empowered the Government to make rules for Part-V. He has further pointed out that in exercise of power under section 152 of the Act, 1950 the Tenancy Rules, 1954 (hereinafter referred to as the Rules, 1954), was framed. Section 144 of the Act, 1950 has given power to the Government to make an order to prepare or revise the record-o f-rights in accordance with the Rules. Chapter-VI consisting of rules 26-35 of the Rules, 1954 has provided detailed procedure for revision of record-of-rights, rules 27 and 27A thereof have laid down almost the same procedure as was made by rule 49 of the Rules made under the B.T. Act. 

 28. There is no dispute that after whole-sale acquisition of the rent receiving interests with effect from the 14th April, 1956 including the Sylhet District (till 1984 Sunamganj was part of the Sylhet District), preparation of fresh rent roll, compensation assessment roll and fresh record-of-rights was required. Chapter-IV, Part-IV of the Act, 1950 has provided for preparation of record-of-rights and section 17 has authorized the Government to make an order for preparation of such record-of-rights. Section 18 of the Act, 1950 has provided for prescribing the particulars to be included in such record-of-rights and section 19 has provided for draft publication, objection, appeal and final publication of such record-of-rights. Rules were framed under Part- IV called the State Acquisition Rule, 1951. Chapter-IV of the said Rules consisting rules 17-38 has provided for preparation and publication of record-of-rights. Sections 32 to 46 in Chapter-V of the Act, 1950 have provided fine preparation of compensation assessment roll and acquisition of rent receiving interests. Section 46 of the Act, 1950 has provided for modification of the record-of-rights prepared under Chapter-IV by eliminating the entire chain of interest of rent receivers and then for reprint and distribution of the record-of-rights. Part II Chapter II, Part III Chapter III, Part IV, Chapters VA, VI to X1 of the Act, 1950 are with regard to acquisition of rent receiving interests and for payment, of compensation for such acquisition. Sections 81 to 143 of the Act have dealt with class, status, right and liabilities of tenants, enhancement and reduction of rents, collection and realisation of rent, subdivision and amalgamation holdings and maintenance of Record of rights. Section 144 of the Act and subsequently added section 144A (inserted by amendment, 1967) are in Part- V. Chapter-XVII in Part-V of the Act has provided for maintenance and revision of the record-of-rights and a presumption of correctness has been attached to the revised record-o rights. Section 152 has empowered the: Government to make rules for Part-V and in exercise of the said power the Rules, 1954 was framed. It is also pertinent to mention that Chapters l-IV of the Rules, 1954 were published in the Dacca Gazette on 7th April, 1955 and Chapters V-IX of the Rules were published in the Dacca Gazette on 14th August, 1955.
